hero_description: A turquoise river flowing through Tenorio Volcano National Park, one of Costa Rica's most magical natural wonders.
description: Río Celeste is one of Costa Rica's most photographed natural attractions. The river's striking turquoise color is created by a natural chemical reaction where two volcanic streams converge inside Tenorio Volcano National Park.
why_visit: Río Celeste is one of Costa Rica's most visually stunning natural wonders. The river runs a brilliant electric blue, the result of volcanic minerals mixing in the waters of Tenorio Volcano National Park. The color is completely natural, no filter required.

A hike through Tenorio National Park leads to the river, a spectacular waterfall, hot springs and wildlife-rich forest. It is one of the most rewarding full-day excursions available from either Guanacaste or La Fortuna.
highlights: Naturally turquoise river, a unique volcanic phenomenon
Río Celeste Waterfall accessible by a scenic forest trail
Rich wildlife: toucans, sloths, howler monkeys and poison dart frogs
Natural thermal hot springs along the riverbank
Tenorio Volcano National Park, pristine and relatively uncrowded
Combinable with La Fortuna or Guanacaste beach stays
considerations: Approximately 2.5 hours from Liberia Airport, best enjoyed as a full-day excursion
The trail can be muddy and slippery during the rainy season
Visitor numbers are limited inside the national park, advance booking is recommended

faq.a: The turquoise color is caused by a natural optical phenomenon: volcanic minerals called aluminosilicates precipitate when two streams mix, scattering light and creating the vivid blue appearance.

faq.q: Can I swim in Río Celeste?
faq.a: Swimming is not permitted inside Tenorio National Park to protect the ecosystem. However, some areas along tubing routes offer water activities outside the park boundaries.

faq.q: How do I get to Río Celeste from Guanacaste?
faq.a: The most comfortable option is a private tour or transfer, which takes approximately 2.5 hours from Liberia Airport. Most visitors combine it with a guided hike through the national park.

faq.q: Is the hike to Río Celeste difficult?
faq.a: The trail is moderate: about 4 km round trip with some uneven terrain and roots. Good walking shoes are recommended. Most healthy adults complete it comfortably.
